title: I made a cozy merge idler where every blob is real soft-body jelly.
author: Carter5on
selftext:
Hi everyone! My name is Vaggelis and I'm a professional designer and artist for games. I'm currently working on my fifth solo game called BlobBobbing.  
  
BlobBobbing is a cozy merge idler. You drag squishy blobs onto their twins and they fuse into rarer, shinier blobs. Every blob runs on real soft-body physics, so they wobble, stretch and bounce like jelly, and the nest keeps earning while you are away.

  
The game currently features:

\- 12 blobs to discover (plus a secret one).

\- Golden Rush: a golden blob drops in and you have to grab it before it gets away.  
(inspired by the Treasure Goblin in games like Diablo.)

\- Melt Down prestige with 8 mutations.

\- Photo Mode, Dark Mode, Immersive Mode (it hides the UI), and Color-Blind Mode.

\- Works fully offline with mouse only.



It comes out December 7 and a free demo is coming soon.  
I'd love to hear what you think, especially about the squish feel.  


Steam: [https://store.steampowered.com/app/5448900/BlobBobbing/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5448900/BlobBobbing/)

  
Thank you very much!

comments.author: EntropyMonkey
comments.body: How long did you work on this, and what was the budget? Honestly, I'm not sure if people will actually buy it. The way the blobs merge looks super underwhelming right now; I'd definitely put some more work into that part.

replies.author: Carter5on
replies.body: This month, and it will be in development until December. The budget is around €205,98. €69 for Claude, €15 for ElevenLabs, €33,48 for Suno, €88,50 for Steam Fee. VAT included for all. However, these subscriptions are not just for this project. I am using them for work and my other projects.

replies.author: EntropyMonkey
replies.body: That's interesting. Did the other four titles you previously released perform well commercially? Are you satisfied with the sales results?

replies.author: Carter5on
replies.body: They did not, but I only presented them on Linkedin and Facebook. I just needed to get them out. I used AI on those only for music and sfx. The graphic were hand-made on paper. The code was GDscript in Godot 3. I was not satisfied with their performace, but it's my fault for making them too cheap and short.

replies.author: EntropyMonkey
replies.body: Then I wish you the best of luck with the new project!

comments.author: No-Blacksmith7127
comments.body: I feel like I'd spend more time messing around with the squishy blobs than actually playing the game lol. The soft-body physics are a nice touch. You should drop the demo on r/OpenLobby when it's ready too, I'd love to check it out!

replies.author: Carter5on
replies.body: I will check it out. Thank you.
